concepts: Permission tree (tasks)

Permissions are organised as a tree: feature groups (e.g. Attendance Management, Employee Master, Reports) contain features, each with action leaves like Create, Modify, Cancel, Delete, View, Download or Upload. The codes in brackets (e.g. 2.1.1) are the permission codes saved against the role.
Auto-selected View

When you tick any action on a feature, its View permission is automatically ticked and disabled, because you must be able to view a feature to act on it. Unticking all other actions releases View again.
MFA Always Required / Allow Trusted Device
Per-role security flags. MFA Always Required forces multi-factor authentication for users with this role; Allow Trusted Device lets them mark a device as trusted to reduce repeat MFA prompts.

title: IP Security
summary: Controls which networks/IP addresses can access the application: set the default Allow or Deny policy, enable IP restriction per feature, and maintain the list of allowed/denied IP rules.

concepts: Default restriction type (Allow vs Deny)

The baseline policy for IP access. Allow = a whitelist: only IPs you explicitly add as Allow can reach the app. Deny = a blacklist: the IPs you add as Deny are blocked and everyone else is allowed. Individual rules in the list refine this baseline.
IP restriction per feature

IP restriction can be switched on or off per feature (e.g. Attendance, Global). The toggle on each feature card enables/disables enforcement for that feature only, and the change is saved as soon as you flip it.
Address type: Range vs Specific

A rule can target a Specific single IP address, or a Range defined by a start and end IP (covering every address in between, e.g. a whole office subnet). The dialog shows the relevant IP fields based on which type you pick.
Active vs InActive rule
Each rule has a status. Only Active rules are enforced; setting a rule InActive keeps it in the list for later without applying it, which is safer than deleting and re-creating it.
Allow/Deny rule type

Independent of the address, each rule is tagged Allow (permit this IP/range) or Deny (block it). Together with the default policy, these decide whether a given source IP can use the restricted feature.
rules: The default restriction type (Allow / Deny) sets the baseline policy; individual IP rules then carry the exceptions in the rules list.
Allow as default means only the IPs you configure with type Allow can access (everything else is restricted); Deny as default means the configured Deny IPs are blocked and the rest are allowed.
IP restriction is applied per feature via each feature's Enable/Disable toggle — turning a feature off means it is not IP-restricted; toggling it saves immediately and shows the server message.
Adding/editing a rule requires Name, Restriction Type, Address Type and Description; the IP fields depend on the Address Type (Specific IP, or Range start + Range end).
Server-side validation rejects bad input per field — e.g. invalid Specific IP, invalid Range End IP, or a missing status ("Please give the status").
Deleting a rule goes through a confirmation dialog before it is removed.
A rule's status is shown as Active or InActive in the grid; only the rules you intend should be Active.
tips: Set the default policy first, then add the minimum set of rules needed — fewer, clearer rules are easier to audit.
Use Specific for a single machine/office IP and Range when a whole subnet should be covered.

concepts: Per-company settings

Notification settings are not global; each company has its own set. Always confirm the right company is selected at the top before you toggle anything, because your changes save against that company only.
Consecutive days threshold
For timesheet reminders, the number you enter is how many days in a row an employee must miss submitting a timesheet before that reminder fires. A higher number means fewer, later reminders.
Recipient-based timesheet reminders

The same "not submitted" event can notify different people — the Project Owner, Delivery Head, Project Manager, Reporting Manager, and/or the employee. Each recipient has its own toggle and its own day count, so you can escalate to managers and remind employees independently.
IT Declaration notifications

These relate to Income Tax (investment) declarations: one toggle opens the declaration notification, and a separate reminder toggle sends a nudge 5 days before the declaration window closes so employees do not miss the deadline.

title: Manage Ticketing Details
summary: Configures Help Desk routing: define ticket categories and sub-categories, then map each category/sub-category to the authority who should handle it, scoped by company, location, grade, department, designation, employment type and section, with a priority TAT and a forward route.
next: Start on Category Master - select or add the category and sub-category you want to route, then move to Authority Assign to map it to an authority.
can: Category Master step: pick a category and its sub-category, or Add Category / Add Sub Category

Save the rule to create a new Help Desk configuration, or edit an existing one

Edit or delete an existing routing rule from the list
concepts: Category vs Sub Category

Categories are the top-level buckets a help-desk ticket can belong to (e.g. Payroll, HR, IT). Sub Categories are the finer classifications under a category. Employees pick these when raising a ticket, and the routing rules here decide who handles each combination.
Authority
The employee (or employees) who receive and resolve tickets matching a rule. Assigning the right authority per category/scope ensures a raised ticket lands with the person responsible for that area.
Scope (Company / Location / Grade / Department / Designation / Employment Type / Section)

The audience a routing rule applies to. The same category can be routed to different authorities for different groups by setting these scopes; selecting all options for a scope stores "-1" meaning "applies to all".
Priority & TAT

Priority (e.g. High / Medium / Low) plus a TAT time and period (Minutes / Hours / Days) define the resolution target for tickets matched by the rule. This TAT is what the Help Desk screen later checks to flag whether a closed ticket met its SLA.
Forward To
The default forward route for the rule - where a ticket can be escalated/handed on if the primary authority cannot resolve it.
rules: Every field on the Authority Assign form is required (Category, Sub Category, Company, Location, Grade, Department, Designation, Employment Type, Priority, TAT time, Authority, Section and Forward To) - Save validates and marks all fields touched if anything is missing.
Sub Category only loads after a Category is chosen; picking it first shows "Please Select Category", and a category with none shows "There is No SubCategories".
Sections are driven by the selected Department(s); choosing a section without a department shows "Please Select Department".
When you select ALL options for a scope (e.g. all departments / all locations), the rule is saved with the "-1" = All sentinel instead of every id.
Adding a Category requires a name and description; adding a Sub Category requires a name, description and parent category.
Deleting a rule goes through a confirmation dialog before the authority mapping is removed.
Only authorities whose employee status is active (statusType E) are offered in the Authority dropdown.

Period basis and Embedded counting

Before/After Period sets whether leave accrues relative to the start or end of the period. Embedded counts weekoffs/holidays inside the leave span; Prefix/Postfix Embedded count those immediately before/after the leave.
Encashment, carry-forward and negative balance
Encashable pays out unused leave within a min/max band; Carry Forward rolls a capped number of days into the next cycle; Negative Leaves lets the balance go below zero up to a defined limit.

Special leave accrues based on working a target weekday across selected week numbers each month, with its own validity window, monthly accrual count, a block weekday on which it cannot be submitted, and holiday handling.

PT is a state levy charged as a flat amount per salary band, not a percentage. Each slab maps a salary range (Low to High) to a fixed Tax Amount.
State-specific rules
PT rates, slabs, frequency and exemptions vary by Indian state, so each PT rule is tied to a specific state and registration (PT) number.
Deduction period
Some states deduct PT monthly; others half-yearly with a defined start month (January or April). Monthly disables the Start month; Half Yearly requires it.

Each Tax Rule row carries a New Regime flag. New-regime rules apply when an employee opts for the new tax regime; un-flagged rules belong to the old regime, so a section can hold separate slabs for each.

IT sections (e.g. Section 10, 80C) are the buckets exemptions and deductions fall into. Mapping links each salary allowance/deduction to a section so payroll knows which section a component reduces tax under.
Projection vs Actual period
Projection period estimates annual income and TDS early in the year (and for new joiners); Actual period reflects realised figures for final computation. Both are constrained to the April-March year.

concepts: TDS EMI (monthly installment)

TDS (Tax Deducted at Source) on salary is collected monthly. This screen takes the employee's annual tax-to-pay and splits it into month-wise installments (EMI) from April to March, so payroll deducts the right amount each month.
Projection vs Actuals

Projection mode estimates the full-year tax and the planned monthly split based on declared income/exemptions. Actuals mode reflects what has actually been processed in payroll, so you can compare planned vs deducted.
Tax computation columns

Each row breaks the tax down: Total Gross Income, Exemptions and Standard Deduction give Taxable Income; Tax, Rebate, Cess, Surcharge and Marginal Relief give Total Tax; minus Tax Paid (incl. previous-employer/other-income TDS) gives Tax to Pay, which is what the months must add up to.
Editable vs locked months
Months whose payroll is already processed are locked (read-only). Only the remaining open months can be edited, and the balance tax is distributed across just those months.
Auto-redistribution

When you set one month's amount, the screen recalculates the leftover tax (Tax to Pay minus what is already fixed) and spreads it evenly across the other editable months, highlighting the recomputed cells so the year still totals correctly.
Tax regime (Old / New)

Each employee's tax is computed under their chosen regime (Old or New), shown in the Regime column. The regime determines which exemptions/slabs apply, which is why two employees with the same gross can have different tax.
Bulk Update result

Update EMI sends all loaded employees to the server in batches of 100 with a live progress bar, then shows a result dialog listing each employee with whether their EMI saved successfully and any message.

A ticket starts Open when raised, becomes In Progress once an authority replies, and is Closed when resolved. A closed ticket can be Re-Opened if the issue recurs, which puts it back into the active queue.

Reply posts a message and keeps the ticket open for further conversation. Reply & Close posts your message and closes the ticket in one step. Both add your message (and any attachments) to the ticket timeline.

A record of how many hours you worked on a given day, broken down by project and task. Each entry is one block of work; the calendar and KPI strip add them up per day, per week and per month.

A Client is the customer the work is for, a Project is a piece of work delivered for that client, and a Task is a specific activity inside the project. When clients are enabled you choose Client -> Project -> Task in that order; otherwise you go straight to Project -> Task.

concepts: Asset Group vs Asset Type vs Asset Store

An Asset Group is the broad category (e.g. IT Equipment). An Asset Type is a specific kind within a group (e.g. Laptop) carrying rules like consumable, max quantity, return period and serial-number requirement. An Asset Store is a physical/logical stock location, owned by a Super User, from which stock is issued.
Consumable vs Non-Consumable

Consumable assets (e.g. stationery) are not expected back, so they have no return period. Non-Consumable assets (e.g. laptops) are tracked for return; they carry a Return Period and unit, and the return/recall flow applies to them.
Serial number requirement

An asset type can require a unique serial number per item. When required, each stock item is tracked individually by its serial/service tag, which is what links a specific physical unit to the employee it is assigned to.
Return Period
The time within which a non-consumable asset is expected to be returned. It is set on the asset type (a positive number plus a unit) and drives return tracking once the asset is assigned.
Stock vs assigned asset

Stock is an item held in a store and not yet given out. Assigning it to an employee turns it into an assigned asset that appears on that employee's Employee Assets tab. Recall pulls it back into stock; Return is the employee-initiated handover back.
Assign / Recall / Return / Receive lifecycle

Assign issues a stock item to an employee. Return is raised against an assigned asset (with a comment) and marks it Pending Return. Recall lets the authority pull an asset back. The receiving authority then confirms receipt to close the loop and return the item to stock.
Store Super User & Participants

A store has a Super User (the owner/manager responsible for its stock) and Participants (others who can operate it). Being a store manager also unlocks the Add Stocks tab even without the general 25.1 permission.

concepts: Salary advance

An advance is money paid to you upfront and then recovered from your future salary in instalments. Unlike a loan it is typically interest-free — you repay only the principal, split evenly across the chosen number of months.
EMI (instalment)

The fixed amount deducted from your salary each month until the advance is fully repaid. Here it is simply the advance amount divided by the number of installments (rounded up), so a higher number of installments means a smaller monthly deduction.
Recovery / repayment from salary

Once an advance is approved and disbursed, each month’s EMI is automatically deducted (recovered) from your pay. The Outstanding Balance and EMIs-Paid figures track how much is left and how many instalments have already been recovered.
Advance status lifecycle

An advance moves from Apply (you submit the application) to Approval (Pending until an approver acts, then Approved) to Recovery (instalments deducted each month) and finally Closed once the full amount is repaid. The status chip on each card and the Active vs Closed counts in the summary reflect this lifecycle.

The fixed amount you repay each month. The screen computes it from the loan amount, annual interest rate and number of instalments using the standard reducing-balance formula; for a 0% interest loan it is simply the amount divided by the number of instalments.

How many monthly instalments the loan runs for (1 to 500). It sets the loan duration in months and, together with the start month, determines the end month automatically.

concepts: Local Claim (reimbursement)

A request to be paid back for a local business expense such as travel, food or other costs. You record the reason, mode, travel date, route/distance and amount; once approved and paid by HR it is "settled".
Claim status lifecycle

Waiting for Submission (a draft you have saved but not sent) -> Pending (sent and awaiting approval) -> Approved (cleared by approvers, not yet paid) or Rejected (sent back - you can edit and resend). After approval HR settles it, moving it to Paid in Cash, Paid via Bank or Cheque Paid.
Send For Approval

Submits a draft (or a previously Rejected) claim into the approval workflow. You can send one claim from its row, or tick several Waiting for Submission rows and submit them together; a remarks dialog lets you add a note before sending.
Mode

The expense type for the claim (e.g. a travel mode, Food, or Others). Travel modes require From / To / Distance and can auto-calculate the amount from a per-km rate; Food and Others hide the location fields. Some modes also require a supporting bill.
Settled (Cash / Bank / Cheque)
How an approved claim was finally paid. The Settled summary card breaks the paid total down into Cash, Bank and Cheque so you can see how each claim was reimbursed.
rules: A claim can only be edited while it has no status (draft) or is Rejected - any other status shows "You cannot edit this claim."
A claim can only be sent for approval while it is a draft or Rejected - otherwise it is blocked with "This claim already has status ... You cannot send it again."
Bulk Send For Approval needs at least one row selected, else "Please select at least one claim".
For travel modes (not Food / Others) From, To and Distance are required; the amount may be auto-calculated from distance x the per-km rate and can be locked for that mode.
When a mode requires a document, you must attach a bill before the claim can be saved ("Please upload required document").
A claim becomes Settled only after HR pays it via Cash, Bank or Cheque on the Claim Settlement screen.
tips: Use the status chips to focus - Waiting for Submission shows your drafts ready to send; Rejected shows what you can fix and resend.

concepts: Headcount
The total number of active employees in the selected month for your filtered population, shown with a male/female breakdown and each gender's share as a percentage of the total (the diversity ratio).
Diversity ratio (Male / Female %)
The proportion of the headcount that is male versus female, displayed beside the raw male and female counts so you can gauge gender balance for the selected group and period.
Gross / Compensation

Total gross pay for the population, with its period-over-period change as a percentage and a Gain/Loss trend flag. The Gross chart plots Actual vs Earned gross month by month so you can see cost-to-company movement over the selected window.
Salary Changes vs Loss of Pay

Salary Changes summarises the salary amount, its percentage change, a trend flag and the count of affected employees. Loss of Pay (LOP) is the deduction value for unpaid absence, with its own amount, percentage, trend and employee count.
Attrition Rate
How many people left relative to the workforce in the period, shown as a count plus a percentage and a Gain/Loss trend versus the prior period. A rising attrition rate signals retention risk.
Joinees vs Resignees
Joinees are employees who started and Resignees are those who left in the period. The trend chart overlays both as splines so you can see whether hiring is keeping pace with exits.

concepts: Reportee scope tabs

Direct Reportees shows only your immediate reportees (Y); Indirect Reportees shows the reportees of your direct reportees, one level down (L2); All Reportees shows everyone in your reporting hierarchy (N). The selected scope is applied to every panel and reloads the data.

concepts: Attended (Present) vs Absent

Attended counts the days you were physically present (and in the details dialog, Physical Present). Absents counts working days with no presence recorded. Both are categories in the donut and rows in the Quick Summary.
On Leave (Leaves)
Days covered by an approved leave for the period, shown as the Leaves slice/row. These are distinct from Weekly Offs and Holidays, which are non-working days rather than consumed leave.
Late Entries / Late Hours / Late Deductions

Late Entries (lateInDays) is the count of days you clocked in after your shift start. Late Hours is the total late duration, and Late Deductions is the leave deducted as a penalty for repeated lateness. These appear in the View Attendance details dialog.
Attendance percentage

Each metric's percentage is its value divided by Total Days for the period (e.g. Paid Days / Total Days). It is what colours the accent bar in the Quick Summary and sizes each donut slice. Hour-based metrics show no percentage.
Paid Days
The number of days you are paid for in the period - typically present days plus paid leaves, weekly offs and holidays. It is the primary metric the summary progress indicator tracks.
Weekly Offs vs Rest Days

Weekly Offs are your scheduled non-working days. Rest Days is the same idea shown under a different label and only appears (in the details dialog) when your global setting WeeklyOffShowAsRestday is enabled.
C-off / Comp Off
Compensatory off - leave earned for working on an off day or holiday. It shows as the C-off slice in the donut and as Comp Off in the View Attendance details.

concepts: MIS
Management Information reports such as Employee Listing and Attrition, plus any custom MIS reports configured for your company.
Payroll
Pay-related outputs such as Bank Transfer, Accounting JV, Tally JV, Pay Register, Arrears, Increment, Variance and Gratuity reports.
Statutory
Compliance files and challans such as PT Challan (state wise), ESI Monthly Upload and PF ECR.
Income Tax
Tax-related reports for the selected year, including any custom Income Tax reports configured for your company.
Analytics
Insight reports such as the Customizable Report and Asset Overall Summary, plus any custom analytics reports.
Attendance
Time-and-leave reports such as Swipe, Web Login, Raw Punches, Enhanced Monthly Swipe, Leaves Summary and Leave Utilized reports.
Favourites
A pinned shortlist of reports you star. They appear in the Favourites panel so you can launch them without opening the category card each time.
Static vs Dynamic reports
Static reports are built into the product, while dynamic reports are configured for your company; both open the same parameter form when launched.
